plain: Harmful or damaging, as to a person's case or rights

webster.text: Biased or blinded by prejudices; as a prejudicial eye.

more.text: Hurtful; mischievous; injurious; disadvantageous; detrimental; tending to obstruct or impair.

example.quote: Even good men in office, in time, imperceptibly lose sight of the people, and gradually fall into measures prejudicial to them.
example.cite: Letters from the Federal Farmer to the Republican, Letter XI, Jan. 10, 1788
